<thought>Based on the ESI‑MS spectrum the most intense ion is at m/z ≈ 233.96 with a clear M + 2 isotopic peak (≈ 24 % of the base peak), indicating the presence of a single chlorine atom. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 232.96 Da. Removing the mass of ^35Cl (34.969 Da) leaves ≈ 197.99 Da, which is best matched by a C₉H₁₀O₅ fragment (exact mass ≈ 198.05 Da). Adding the chlorine atom yields a molecular formula that fits the observed isotopic pattern and mass. 

Thus the most plausible molecular formula for the compound is **C9H10O5Cl**.
